fullPassage: How much time do you spend sitting per day? Studies have found that one-third of the global population aged fifteen years and older engage in insufficient physical activity. In particular, teenagers spend too much of their time sitting down and seldom do they engage in active physical activities on a regular basis. The scientific community has even coined the term “sitting disease” for this phenomenon in order to represent the harmful health effects that result from long periods of sitting. The longer you sit, the more exposed you are to the dangers of obesity, heart disease, diabetes, and even depression. Walking, according to health experts, is one of the safest, easiest, and cheapest forms of exercise to combat sitting disease. Walking is not only a simple way to avoid the harmful effects of sitting disease, but it also has other health benefits. You may already be aware of the health benefits of walking, such as bone strengthening, blood pressure reduction, and improved heart health. But did you know that walking can help lower your cravings for sugary foods? According to research by the University of Exeter, taking daily walks for fifteen minutes can cut chocolate consumption in half. This is because frequent physical activity can enhance brain function, making it easier to limit our consumption of sweet foods such as chocolate. Moreover, walking can keep you from getting sick during the cold and flu season. A study found that people who walked for at least twenty minutes a day, five days a week, had 43% fewer sick days than those who exercised once a week or less. And even if they did get sick, it was for a shorter period of time with milder symptoms. This is primarily due to the improved immune system that results from walking regularly. In addition to the physical benefits, walking has been found to improve our creativity. Researchers at Stanford University presented data on the association between walking and creativity. The participants who walked for five to sixteen minutes showed an average increase in creativity, compared to those who remained sitting. This was mainly because the areas of the brain responsible for learning and memory worked more efficiently when people walked. It is no wonder that Steve Jobs came up with some of his most brilliant ideas while walking, and much of his company’s design process was developed during walking meetings with his staff. Despite the importance and benefits of walking, as students, finding the time to include it in your daily lives may appear challenging or bothersome. Even when you have time, you may dismiss the thought of walking. Instead of walking, you might prefer to connect with friends on social media or watch TV at home. But walking can be fun. Here are some simple ways to make walking enjoyable for you. Get Your Groove On A “music walk” is a great way to make walking feel less like a workout. All you will need is a smartphone with a music streaming app and a good pair of walking shoes. Additionally, you can bring a pair of earphones in case other people are disturbed or annoyed by your music. You can create playlists for different moods or circumstances. Are you going for a walk at sunset by the lake? Create a playlist of calm and relaxing tunes to help you appreciate the peaceful environment. Going for a power walk to enjoy the autumn breeze? Fill your playlist with energetic songs that will motivate you to walk harder. So grab your phone, put on your walking shoes, and let the rhythm move you! Walk and Talk Having a walking buddy can really motivate you to lace up the sneakers if you feel lonely or bored when walking alone. When you make plans to walk with a friend, you are more likely to follow through since you do not want to let your friend down. Additionally, having someone to chat with can help you forget that you are even exercising, making the time fly by. You will find yourself so engaged in conversation that you will not even realize how far you have walked. Moreover, with a friend by your side, you will have someone to share the beauty of your surroundings with, making your walks more exciting and engaging. Make It a Challenge Set a goal for the number of steps you want to take per day or week, and then work toward it. Using a smartphone app, keep track of your daily steps. Increasing your step count over a few weeks would be challenging yet rewarding. You do not need to set aside time for this walking challenge. You can take part in the challenge by walking during your lunch break, taking the stairs instead of the elevator, or walking in place while brushing your teeth. You can even make walking a social media challenge and get others to join you.

det.korean: ① make walking to feel → make walking feel: 사역동사 make는 목적격보어로 동사원형을 쓴다
det.analysis:
❌ ① make walking to feel → make walking feel: make가 '~하게 하다'라는 사역동사로 쓰이면 뒤에 오는 동사는 to 없이 동사원형을 써요. 그래서 'make walking feel(걷기가 ~하게 느껴지게 만들다)'이 맞고 'to feel'은 틀려요 ← 정답

✅ ② All you will need is: 'All (that) you will need'가 하나의 단수 주어라서 단수 동사 is가 알맞아요

✅ ③ are disturbed or annoyed: '다른 사람들이 방해받거나 짜증나다'라는 수동의 뜻이라 'be동사 + p.p.' 수동태로 알맞아요

✅ ④ create playlists: 'You can create playlists'에서 조동사 can 뒤 동사원형으로 알맞아요
det.tip: 사역동사 make + 목적어 + 동사원형(feel). to feel 불가

✅ ② songs that will motivate: 앞의 명사 songs를 꾸미는 주격 관계대명사 that으로 알맞아요

det.korean: ② did got sick → did get sick: 조동사 did 뒤에는 동사원형을 쓴다
det.analysis:
✅ ① than those who exercised: 'fewer sick days than those who exercised'에서 비교 대상을 나타내는 'than those who ~(~한 사람들보다)'로 알맞아요

❌ ② did got sick → did get sick: 여기서 did는 동사를 강조하는 조동사예요. 조동사(did) 뒤에는 반드시 동사원형이 오므로 'did get(정말 아팠다)'이 맞고, 과거형 got을 쓴 'did got'은 틀려요 ← 정답

✅ ③ that results from walking: 앞의 명사 'the improved immune system'(단수)을 꾸미는 주격 관계대명사 that이고, 선행사가 단수라 results로 수를 맞춰 알맞아요

✅ ④ has been found to improve: 'walking has been found to improve'에서 현재완료 수동태(have been p.p.)로 알맞아요

det.korean: ③ bored in conversation → engaged in conversation: 대화에 '푹 빠져' 얼마나 걸었는지도 모른다
det.analysis:
✅ ① lonely: 혼자 걸으면 '외롭거나(lonely)' 지루할 수 있어 친구가 동기를 준다는 문맥에 알맞아요

✅ ② likely: 친구와 걷기로 약속하면 실천할 '가능성이 높다(likely)'는 문맥에 알맞아요

❌ ③ bored in conversation → engaged in conversation: 뒤에 '얼마나 멀리 걸었는지조차 깨닫지 못한다'가 이어지므로, 대화에 '푹 빠진(engaged)' 상태여야 시간 가는 줄 모르는 거예요. bored(지루한)라면 걸은 거리를 오히려 잘 느꼈을 테니 정반대라 어긋나요 ← 정답

❌ ③ 스마트폰 앱은 도전을 돕는 도구로 잠깐 언급될 뿐 주제가 아니에요

❌ ④ 스티브 잡스 사례는 걷기의 창의력 효과를 보여 주는 예시일 뿐 전체 주제가 아니에요

questions.passage: How much time do you spend sitting per day?  Studies have found that one-third of the global population aged fifteen years and older engage in insufficient physical activity.  In particular, teenagers spend too much of their time sitting down and seldom do they engage in active physical activities on a regular basis.  The scientific community has even coined the term “sitting disease” for this phenomenon in order to represent the harmful health effects that result from long periods of sitting.  The longer you sit, the more exposed you are to the dangers of obesity, heart disease, diabetes, and even depression.  Walking, according to health experts, is one of the safest, easiest, and cheapest forms of exercise to combat sitting disease.  Walking is not only a simple way to avoid the harmful effects of sitting disease, but it also has other health benefits.  You may already be aware of the health benefits of walking, such as bone strengthening, blood pressure reduction, and improved heart health.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ Step by Step: Why Walking Is Worth It(한 걸음씩: 걷기가 그만한 가치가 있는 이유)
det.analysis:
글은 오래 앉아 있는 것의 위험을 짚고, 걷기의 여러 이점과 걷기를 즐기는 방법을 소개해요.

❌ ① The Hidden Dangers of Too Much Exercise(과도한 운동의 숨은 위험): 글은 운동이 '지나친' 것을 경고하지 않아요

❌ ② How Smartphones Are Ruining Teenagers' Health(스마트폰이 십대 건강을 망치는 방식): 스마트폰은 걷기를 돕는 도구로 나올 뿐이에요

❌ ③ Sitting Disease: An Illness That Has No Cure(앉아 있는 병: 치료법이 없는 질병): 글은 걷기라는 해법을 제시하므로 '치료법이 없다'는 어긋나요

✅ ④ Step by Step: Why Walking Is Worth It(한 걸음씩: 걷기가 그만한 가치가 있는 이유): 걷기의 이점과 실천법을 담은 글 전체를 압축한 제목이에요 ← 정답
det.tip: 제목 = 걷기가 가치 있는 이유(이점 + 실천법)

ch: The Hidden Dangers of Too Much Exercise
How Smartphones Are Ruining Teenagers' Health
Sitting Disease: An Illness That Has No Cure
Step by Step: Why Walking Is Worth It

questions.passage: Walk and Talk Having a walking buddy can really motivate you to <u>lace up the sneakers</u> if you feel lonely or bored when walking alone.  When you make plans to walk with a friend, you are more likely to follow through since you do not want to let your friend down.  Additionally, having someone to chat with can help you forget that you are even exercising, making the time fly by.  You will find yourself so engaged in conversation that you will not even realize how far you have walked.  Moreover, with a friend by your side, you will have someone to share the beauty of your surroundings with, making your walks more exciting and engaging.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 lace up the sneakers가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ 걷기(운동)를 시작하다
det.analysis:
밑줄 문장: 'Having a walking buddy can really motivate you to lace up the sneakers if you feel lonely or bored when walking alone.'(혼자 걸을 때 외롭거나 지루하면, 함께 걷는 친구가 운동화 끈을 묶도록 정말 동기를 줄 수 있다). '운동화 끈을 묶다(lace up the sneakers)'는 곧 '걷기(운동)를 시작하다'를 비유적으로 나타내는 표현이에요.

❌ ① 새 운동화를 사러 가다: 구매와는 무관해요

❌ ② 친구와 크게 다투다: 문맥과 전혀 관련 없어요

✅ ③ 걷기(운동)를 시작하다: 운동화 끈을 묶는다는 것은 곧 걸으러 나선다는 뜻이에요 ← 정답

❌ ④ 산책을 도중에 포기하다: 오히려 걷도록 동기를 준다는 흐름과 반대예요
det.tip: lace up the sneakers(운동화 끈을 묶다) = 걷기(운동)를 시작하다

questions.passage: In addition to the physical benefits, walking has been found to improve our creativity.  Researchers at Stanford University presented data on the association between walking and creativity.  The participants who walked for five to sixteen minutes showed an average increase in creativity, compared to those who remained sitting.  This was mainly because the areas of the brain responsible for learning and memory worked more efficiently when people walked.  It is no wonder that Steve Jobs came up with some of <u>his</u> most brilliant ideas while walking, and much of his company’s design process was developed during walking meetings with his staff.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 his가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① 스티브 잡스(Steve Jobs)
det.analysis:
밑줄 문장: 'It is no wonder that Steve Jobs came up with some of his most brilliant ideas while walking, and much of his company's design process was developed during walking meetings with his staff.'(스티브 잡스가 걷는 동안 가장 뛰어난 아이디어를 떠올린 것도, 그의 회사 디자인 과정 상당 부분이 직원들과의 걷기 회의에서 만들어진 것도 놀랍지 않다). 밑줄 친 his는 바로 앞의 Steve Jobs를 가리켜요.

✅ ① 스티브 잡스: his most brilliant ideas = 스티브 잡스의 뛰어난 아이디어 ← 정답

❌ ② 직원들(staff)은 his가 아니라 뒤의 walking meetings의 상대예요

❌ ③ 스탠퍼드 대학 연구진은 앞 문장에 나온 다른 주체예요

❌ ④ 학생들은 이 문장의 지시 대상이 아니에요
det.tip: his most brilliant ideas = Steve Jobs의 아이디어

questions.passage: Make It a Challenge Set a goal for the number of steps you want to take per day or week, and then __________.  Using a smartphone app, keep track of your daily steps.  Increasing your step count over a few weeks would be challenging yet rewarding.  You do not need to set aside time for this walking challenge.  You can take part in the challenge by walking during your lunch break, taking the stairs instead of the elevator, or walking in place while brushing your teeth.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 work toward it(그것을 향해 노력하다)이 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① give it up(그것을 포기하다): 목표를 세운 뒤 포기한다는 것은 도전을 권하는 흐름과 반대예요

✅ ② work toward it(그것을 향해 노력하다): '하루나 일주일에 걷고 싶은 걸음 수 목표를 정하고, 그다음 그것을 향해 노력하라'는 흐름이 자연스러워요 ← 정답

❌ ③ forget about it(그것을 잊어버리다): 목표를 세운 취지와 반대예요

❌ ④ write it down(그것을 적어 두다): 목표 달성을 위한 '실천'과는 초점이 달라요
det.tip: Set a goal ~, and then ___: 목표를 향해 노력하다(work toward it)

questions.passage: But did you know that walking can help lower your cravings for sugary foods?  According to research by the University of Exeter, taking daily walks for fifteen minutes can cut chocolate consumption in half.  This is because frequent physical activity can enhance brain function, making it easier to limit our consumption of sweet foods such as chocolate.  Moreover, __________ during the cold and flu season.  A study found that people who walked for at least twenty minutes a day, five days a week, had 43% fewer sick days than those who exercised once a week or less.  And even if they did get sick, it was for a shorter period of time with milder symptoms.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"걷기는 당신이 아프지 않게 막아 줄 수 있다." (7단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) can, from, getting, keep, sick, walking, you를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: walking can keep you from getting sick
det.analysis:
'막아 주다'는 'keep + 목적어 + from + 동명사(-ing)(…가 ~하는 것을 막다)' 구문으로 나타내요.

먼저 주어와 조동사: walking(걷기는) + can(~할 수 있다) + keep(막다).

무엇을 막는가 하면 you(당신이) 아픈 상태가 되는 것이에요: from + getting + sick(아프게 되는 것으로부터).

순서대로 놓으면 walking / can / keep / you / from / getting / sick.
det.tip: keep A from -ing(A가 ~하지 못하게 하다) / from 뒤에는 동명사 getting

questions.wa: walking can keep you from getting sick
accept: walking can keep you from getting sick

questions.passage: Make It a Challenge Set a goal for the number of steps you want to take per day or week, and then work toward it.  Using a smartphone app, keep track of your daily steps.  Increasing your step count over a few weeks would be challenging yet rewarding.  You do not need to set aside time for this walking challenge.  You can take part in the challenge by walking during your lunch break, taking the stairs instead of the elevator, or walking in place ①<u>while brush</u> your teeth.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①은 어법상 틀렸다. 어법에 맞게 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓰시오. (한 단어, 영어로)

det.korean: while brush → brushing: '~하는 동안'을 뜻하는 while 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)를 쓴다
det.analysis:
밑줄이 있는 문장은 'You can take part in the challenge by walking during your lunch break, taking the stairs instead of the elevator, or walking in place while ①<u>brush</u> your teeth.'예요. '점심시간에 걷거나, 엘리베이터 대신 계단을 이용하거나, 양치질을 하는 동안 제자리에서 걸으며 도전에 참여할 수 있다'는 뜻이에요.

여기서 while은 '~하는 동안'이라는 뜻으로, 뒤에 '주어 + be동사'가 생략된 분사구문이 이어져요. 이때는 동사원형이 아니라 동명사(-ing) 형태를 써야 해요.

그래서 brush가 아니라 brushing으로 고쳐야 맞아요. 앞의 walking, taking과도 흐름이 자연스럽게 이어져요.

정답은 brushing이에요.
det.tip: while + 동명사(-ing): while brushing your teeth(양치질을 하는 동안)

questions.passage: In particular, teenagers spend too much of their time sitting down and seldom do they engage in active physical activities on a regular basis. "당신이 더 오래 앉아 있을수록, 당신은 위험에 더 많이 노출된다." (9단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) are, exposed, longer, more, sit, the, the, you, you를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: the longer you sit, the more exposed you are
det.analysis:
'~하면 할수록 더 …하다'는 'the + 비교급 ~, the + 비교급 …' 구문으로 나타내요.

앞부분 '당신이 더 오래 앉아 있을수록'은 the + 비교급(longer) + 주어(you) + 동사(sit) 순서로: the / longer / you / sit.

뒷부분 '당신은 더 많이 노출된다'도 the + 비교급(more exposed) + 주어(you) + 동사(are) 순서로: the / more / exposed / you / are. exposed는 'be exposed to(~에 노출되다)'의 과거분사예요.

순서대로 이으면 the / longer / you / sit / the / more / exposed / you / are.
det.tip: the 비교급 ~, the 비교급 … (~할수록 더 …하다) / be exposed to(~에 노출되다)

questions.passage: __________.  Get Your Groove On A “music walk” is a great way to make walking feel less like a workout.  All you will need is a smartphone with a music streaming app and a good pair of walking shoes.  Additionally, you can bring a pair of earphones in case other people are disturbed or annoyed by your music.  You can create playlists for different moods or circumstances.

"여기 걷기를 당신에게 즐겁게 만드는 몇 가지 간단한 방법이 있다."

[ are / enjoyable / for / here / make / simple / some / to / walking / ways / you ] (11단어) (영어로)

det.korean: here are some simple ways to make walking enjoyable for you
det.analysis:
'여기 ~이 있다'는 'Here + 동사 + 주어'로 주어와 동사가 도치돼요: here + are + some simple ways(몇 가지 간단한 방법).

어떤 방법인가 하면 '걷기를 즐겁게 만드는' 방법이에요. 이는 앞의 ways를 꾸미는 to부정사구로 나타내요: to + make + walking + enjoyable. make는 사역동사로 'make + 목적어(walking) + 형용사(enjoyable)(걷기를 즐겁게 만들다)' 구조예요.

마지막으로 '당신에게'는 for you로 붙여요.

순서대로 이으면 here / are / some / simple / ways / to / make / walking / enjoyable / for / you.
det.tip: Here are + 주어(도치) / make + 목적어 + 형용사(enjoyable): 걷기를 즐겁게 만들다

"당신은 끝까지 해낼 가능성이 더 높다." (7단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) are, follow, likely, more, through, to, you를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것
